_comment: Source-content verifier configuration. Consumed by scripts/source-verify.py. This file holds ONLY extraction + verification knobs. Network politeness (rate limits, per-host caps, gov-suffix floor, EUR-Lex crawl-delay, excluded hosts, Cloudflare markers, retries, timeouts, user-agent) is NOT duplicated here — source-verify.py loads config/_url-liveness.json for all of that so the two tools share one source of truth. Update with a CHANGELOG entry + one-line rationale per change.

extraction._primary_only: When true, only citations to a primary government / regulated source (gov-suffix OR an entry in scripts/primary-source-allowlist.txt) become claim records. These are the 'citable as fact' claims whose wrongness is most damaging. --include-secondary overrides at the CLI.
extraction._min_salient_values: A citation needs at least this many SALIENT value tokens (percentage / money / statute / specific date — a bare year does not count) in its surrounding claim sentence to be treated as a verifiable claim. Filters out navigation/roster links that carry no number.
extraction._claim_window_chars: Fallback character window around the link used as the claim sentence when the containing line is longer than this.

fetch._min_text_chars: An OK (200) page whose CLEANED body has fewer than this many chars yielded no usable text — a JS-SPA / client-rendered shell or blocked stub. A zero-match fetch this thin is classified SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (indeterminate), NOT TOKENS_ABSENT, so a CORRECT citation to a JS-rendered gov page isn't false-flagged as a missing figure. Conservative on the safe side: a tiny page erring to 'indeterminate' beats a false 'absent'.
fetch._js_spa_hosts: Hosts known to be client-side-rendered (the no-JS fetcher gets an empty shell). A zero-match OK fetch from these is SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE regardless of body length — a backstop to min_text_chars for shells that exceed it. e.g. Hong Kong e-Legislation (the bulk of HK statute-citation false-positives).

pdf._extractor: pdftotext -layout (poppler) preferred for table fidelity; pypdf pure-python fallback; PDF_NO_TEXT if neither extracts (scanned image).
pdf._max_bytes: PDFs must be read in FULL — truncating mid-file (unlike HTML) corrupts the structure and the extractor returns nothing. 12 MB covers gov fee/rate-schedule PDFs with headroom.

linter._comment: check-citations.py flags citations to a bare domain ROOT sitting next to a figure (the page that proves the number is almost never the homepage). Advisory only. Add hosts/URLs here that are legitimate root pointers.

sampling._default_sample: Per-run claim cap handed to the (expensive) LLM verification layer. Selection is FETCH-FREE — scored from extract metadata only — so network stays bounded to the chosen sample. TOKENS_ABSENT is a post-fetch verdict-prior surfaced in the worklist, never a selection key.
